investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T23:52–23:59Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing every required-evidence assertion to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. With 0 preemption victims available and 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector, no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled. This is a cluster-capacity or peer-pod quota constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never starts, the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1344, createAgent call) never returns an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes; preemption also failed ('0/6 nodes available: 2 No preemption victims found').
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=143164, pod stuck unscheduled for 138s before the eval timed out and reported fail.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 145s, latencyMs=148737 — confirms the same capacity constraint blocked a second independent pod request.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 147s, latencyMs=148586 — confirms a third independent pod request was also blocked.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent because the pod never reached a running state and the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1344 (createAgent call) never completed.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1336-1344: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which depends on a schedulable pod; no pod means no agent identity or VM state is ever returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:178-186: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because evidence was never produced.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures.

SECONDARY — peer-pod quota or limit configured too low for the current workload demand: the cluster may have a hard cap on kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations that has been reached, rather than a transient spike in usage.

TERTIARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If those affinity rules are overly restrictive, even modest VM demand would exhaust capacity. This is a contributing factor but does not explain the 'Insufficient' message on its own.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — transient burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads at the time of the eval run (23:52–23:59Z) temporarily consumed all VM slots; capacity may self-recover once existing pods terminate.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1364) never produced a schedulable pod, so the probe timed out without writing any evidence, causing the remote-agent-state contract to report all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) as missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource type, and the remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request stalls until the eval probe times out. This is a resource-capacity or node-affinity configuration problem in the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval infrastructure defect. No evidence of user-traffic or incident signals is present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval layer at this time.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pod VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No remote agent pod was ever scheduled, so the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster (6 nodes total) has exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms no schedulable node exists for the remote agent pod. Because the pod never starts, the eval probe's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1377) never completes, no runtime response is returned, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage, as no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. All three sibling checks report the identical scheduler message, confirming this is a cluster-wide capacity condition at the time of the eval run.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so even if VM capacity were freed, the other 4 nodes remain ineligible. This is expected by design but means the effective scheduling pool is only 2 nodes.

Tertiary — eval probe timeout configuration: the check is configured with outageLatencyMs=420000 (7 min) but the pod was unscheduled for ~147s before the probe surfaced the failure at ~148s latency, suggesting the probe detected the Unschedulable condition and surfaced it early rather than waiting for the full timeout. This is correct behavior but means the failure is reported quickly when the scheduler emits Unschedulable.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node drain, rolling update, or scale-down) that temporarily reduced kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run. No node event or incident signal is present in the evidence to confirm or deny this.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T23:52–23:59Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing every required-evidence assertion to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. With 0 preemption victims available and 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector, no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled. This is a cluster-capacity or peer-pod quota constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never starts, the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1344, createAgent call) never returns an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes; preemption also failed ('0/6 nodes available: 2 No preemption victims found').
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=143164, pod stuck unscheduled for 138s before the eval timed out and reported fail.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 145s, latencyMs=148737 — confirms the same capacity constraint blocked a second independent pod request.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 147s, latencyMs=148586 — confirms a third independent pod request was also blocked.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent because the pod never reached a running state and the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1344 (createAgent call) never completed.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1336-1344: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which depends on a schedulable pod; no pod means no agent identity or VM state is ever returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:178-186: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because evidence was never produced.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures.

SECONDARY — peer-pod quota or limit configured too low for the current workload demand: the cluster may have a hard cap on kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations that has been reached, rather than a transient spike in usage.

TERTIARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If those affinity rules are overly restrictive, even modest VM demand would exhaust capacity. This is a contributing factor but does not explain the 'Insufficient' message on its own.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — transient burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads at the time of the eval run (23:52–23:59Z) temporarily consumed all VM slots; capacity may self-recover once existing pods terminate.

Consider adding a historical pass/fail trend eval for remote-agent-create so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be populated in future runs, enabling faster triage of new vs. sustained failures.

affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes that carry this resource, blocking all remote agent pod creation. Evidence items failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state all confirm this.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check
affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner branch at line 1372-1377 calls createAgent for a remote agent; if the pod cannot be scheduled, no evidence is returned and the expected-output contract (check-expectations.json line 194-197) is entirely unmet.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create eval check (sibling)
affectedAreas.reason: Sibling check failed with the identical scheduler error (sibling.remote-agent-create), confirming the scheduling failure affects all remote agent pod creation attempts.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-state eval check (sibling)
affectedAreas.reason: Sibling check failed with the identical scheduler error (sibling.remote-agent-state), confirming the scheduling failure persisted across sequential eval runs within the same observability window.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature registry entry
affectedAreas.reason: Feature is configured with degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (lines 155-156); with all three checks failing, the feature health threshold for outage is met within the eval system.

recommendedNextActions: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the production cluster immediately: describe the 2 eligible nodes and list all pods consuming VM slots to determine whether capacity is still exhausted.
If VM slots are exhausted by stale or leaked pods (e.g., from previous eval runs that did not clean up), evict or delete those pods to free capacity and re-run the eval to confirm recovery.

If VM slots are exhausted by legitimate workloads, assess whether the kata-capable node pool needs to be scaled out (adding nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity) to accommodate both production workloads and eval probe pods.

Review the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm that eval-created remote agent pods are reliably cleaned up after each run; a cleanup failure could cause VM slot leakage across successive eval runs.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the remote-agent eval probes that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting pod creation, and surfaces a SKIP or WARN status with a descriptive message when capacity is zero, rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe to check if failure persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity constraint is persistent or was transient at the time of the failing run.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe kata-capable nodes to inspect VM slot allocatable vs. used
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether VM slots are exhausted and by how many units, identifying the capacity gap.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe node on each node carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and compare Allocatable to the sum of resource Requests across all pods on those nodes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the production cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies which workloads are consuming the limited VM capacity and whether any are stale, leaked, or eligible for eviction.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl get pods --all-namespaces with a field selector or resource filter to enumerate all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated eval source paths for probe timeout and scheduling-wait logic
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the probe correctly surfaces the scheduler error or whether a longer wait would allow scheduling if capacity frees up.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Review infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs around the createAgent call at line 1377 to confirm how long the probe waits for pod scheduling before surfacing the Unschedulable message.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A subsequent eval run where the remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, and remote-agent-state checks all pass would indicate the capacity constraint was transient and has self-resolved.

kubectl describe on the 2 kata-capable nodes showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots greater than zero at the time of the failing eval run would suggest the scheduler message was erroneous or the pod spec had an additional constraint not reflected in the error.

Evidence that the pod was eventually scheduled and the failure was caused by a timeout in the eval probe's wait logic rather than a true scheduling failure would shift the root cause to probe timeout configuration.

A passing run of local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks during the same window would confirm the failure is isolated to remote (kata peer-pod) scheduling and not a broader API or authentication issue.
Node event logs showing a deliberate drain or scale-down of kata-capable nodes during the eval window would confirm a transient infrastructure event rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on all eligible nodes and fails with a warning when available slots fall below a configured threshold, providing early warning before scheduling failures occur.
Add a remote-agent-cleanup eval check that verifies no orphaned remote agent pods from previous eval runs remain on the cluster after each observability run, catching VM slot leakage proactively.

Add a remote-agent-scheduling-latency eval check that measures the time from pod submission to Running state and warns when scheduling latency exceeds a threshold, distinguishing slow scheduling from outright Unschedulable failures.

Extend the existing remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerMessage, unschedulableReason) so that future failures include machine-readable capacity signals alongside the human-readable message.

evidenceDigest.message: pod stuck unscheduled for 147s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.
